title: Hierarchical provisional slice rescheduler and scaled-throughput steward
author: Sonia Patel
description: Context: Dedicated fleets sometimes need to temporarily re-slice committed capacity to absorb asymmetric tenant demand (e.g. a single tenant spike while other tenants are idle). Motivation: existing warm-pool and reserve mechanisms are conservative and often over-provision or induce tail latency when doing emergency reassignments. This PR introduces a hierarchical provisional slice rescheduler (HPSR) plus a lightweight scaled-throughput steward that together allow short-lived provisional capacity slices to be created, rebalanced, and reclaimed with safety guards and observability. Design summary: 1) Provisional slices are ephemeral capacity assignments with a TTL and a score computed from recent utilization, latency tail, and tenant criticality. 2) HPSR runs in two phases: candidate generation (per-pool local sampler) and global reconciliation (hierarchical coordinator that prefers local rebalances where possible). 3) Steward enforces scaled-throughput constraints per-tenant during provisional periods: soft concurrency caps, token-bucket smoothing, and automatic rollback if error rates or P50/P99 exceed configured thresholds. 4) Spillover lanes: when provisional capacity isn't available in the same pool, HPSR can open a short-lived spillover lane to a cross-pool warmlet with enforced rate limits and transparent fallback routing. 5) Safety: circuit breakers for repeated rebalances, a decay window to prevent oscillation, and leader-elected garbage collection for orphan provisional slices. Backwards compatibility and rollout: feature gated behind remote-config flag "hpsr.enabled"; default disabled for 48h after release. Migration: database schema adds a single KV key for provisional-slice metadata; includes automatic migration on startup. Observability: new metrics (provisional_slice_created, provisional_slice_reclaimed, spillover_lane_opened, steward_throttles, steward_rollbacks) and a small set of traces for cross-pool reconciliation paths. Checklist: - [x] Core rescheduler algorithm implemented - [x] Steward enforcement and rollback wiring - [x] Unit tests for candidate selection + TTL expiry - [x] Integration test simulating tenant spike and spillover lane - [x] Telemetry dashboards and alert rules drafted - [x] Docs: user-facing note in capacity strategies doc - [x] Feature-flagged rollout plan and migration script Commits summary: - initial hpsr controller and local sampler - steward: throughput caps and rollback policy - spillover lane implementation and rate limiter - metrics, tracing hooks, and dashboard json - tests: unit + integration harness - docs: capacity strategies addendum - fix: leader-election edge-case requeue Note: description kept single-string per repo convention.
